text: When the chapter is read with the earlier promise in view, the difference between them narrows. Isaac is named again as the child of the covenant, the son through whom the nations are to be blessed; and the narrator makes of that very promise a test. The scene rests upon a single word, _hineni_, "here I am," which Abraham speaks three times. Its sense alters with each speaking, and each speaking costs him more than the last; for in this scene to stand present before God or before another cannot be parted from loss. He says it first to God, then to Isaac, and last to the angel.
